deployment: reference shape: Microsoft 365 Business Premium tenant (Defender for Business, Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, Entra ID P1) reached through the microsoft-security MCP server; advanced hunting answers the identity and vulnerability tables, while the raw endpoint, email and cloud-app activity tables stay empty at this licence. It is what the server's capability probe binds on a tenant meeting reference.provides, which tools/check_binding.py verifies against the manifest; a probe run against the tenant itself supersedes this file.

asset.cmdb.notes: device role, OS, exposure and tags (defender_get_software for the software inventory); business criticality comes from the SOC Knowledge Base

identity.directory.notes: the IdentityInfo table: department, title, group membership, assigned roles

cases.store.notes: closed incidents and their entities; the 90-day retrospective sweep runs here, never through telemetry

malware.repository.notes: prevalence and first-seen by hash; hashes only leave the environment

decode.notes: encoded PowerShell commands; timestamp_to_utc for time zones

telemetry.endpoint.notes: alert evidence only: there is no query language to translate playbook questions into; every question the evidence does not answer is a visibility gap

ticketing.notes: tuning tickets as incident comments until a ticketing tool is bound

Address and domain reputation are not covered: defender_get_ip_statistics and defender_get_domain_statistics give this tenant's prevalence, not a verdict, so bind reputation.multi_engine for those
